assessment.headline: DAY 30. One month. FII ₹1.13L Cr exodus. But Indian LPG carriers are crossing. The war is both worsening and showing cracks.
assessment.body:
One month into the worst geopolitical crisis since India's independence, the picture is contradictory. On one hand, 2 more Indian LPG carriers crossed Hormuz and discharged cargo — showing India is getting selective passage. On the other, FII outflow hit ₹1,13,810 crore in March — the largest monthly selloff in history. PhonePe halted its IPO. The market is down 12% since January.

The war is widening (Houthis, nuclear strikes on heavy-water + yellowcake facilities, university threats) while simultaneously showing cracks (20 Pakistani ships transiting, indirect talks via Pakistan, Trump extending to April 6). $580 million in suspicious oil futures bets were placed 15 minutes before Trump's Truth Social post — a possible insider trading scandal.

For India's households:
• Excise cut ₹10/L on petrol+diesel — first major relief but 'huge revenue hit'
• Rupee at 94.79 ATL. RBI burned $12-15B. Forex reserves down $19B in 2 weeks
• 91% of LPG from Gulf — still choking. 75% food service depends on LPG = ₹1,200-1,300 Cr/day losses
• Indian crude basket at $125/barrel. Macquarie: 40% chance of $200 oil
• 10 million Indians in Gulf — remittances at risk
• CSMonitor: 'India is the biggest loser in a war it isn't even fighting'

April 6 is 8 days away. The 15-point US plan and Iran's 5-point counter remain far apart. Pakistan is mediating. India is getting some LPG through but it's a fraction of need. The next week determines whether this is the beginning of a resolution — or the prelude to the worst phase yet.
